evidence: Strengths: nearly every criterion names a concrete browser-observable end state (stage, place, order, count, focus via document.activeElement, scroll offset via getBoundingClientRect, 401 status, independent-context readback, restart_app comparison), probes are suffixed per review (functional prompt.md:15, polish prompt.md:14), 'Call back on Fri' is absent from seed_data.json (grep count 0), and visual likert rows carry five described anchors (acceptable craft judgement per skill). Gate rows (render judge.toml:22-24, constraints judge.toml:59-61) are concrete with server-backed independent readback. DEFECT (reported for every instance): many server-side refusal probes are request REPLAYS whose outcome is graded only as 'refused with nothing changed', without requiring the replay to carry the target card's current version or the refusal to be for the rule under test. The brief mandates per-card optimistic concurrency (hireops_rules.md:77-80: a move from an out-of-date board is refused 409), so every conforming server refuses a replay carrying a stale/copied version regardless of whether the tested rule exists. functional prompt.md:17 only says 'repeat its actual shape with the stated change'; the stated changes never include refreshing the version, and protocol C (prompt.md:33) teaches the judge that replaying a captured request is refused for staleness. The golden itself checks version before skip/hired/manager-scope/capacity (solution/app/src/index.js:241 precedes :249, :254, :258, :294), and the captured move body carries version (board.js:184-188), so even on the golden these replays can be refused as stale rather than by the tested rule — the probe does not distinguish an app that enforces the rule from one that does not. Affected instances: (1) hro_observer_readonly (functional judge.toml:172-174) 'replays in the Observer's session of an observed move ... Rafael's identical successful requests are the control' — an identical replay of an already-applied move is stale; (2) hro_candidate_no_staff (:181-183) move replay, same; (3) hro_mgr_other_job (:163-165) Bill's replayed J1 move; (4) hro_mgr_early_refused (:154-156) replay legs; (5) hro_move_one_stage (:55-57) skip leg 'if not offered, by replay'; (6) hro_reject_hired (:91-93) replay leg; (7) hro_interview_full (:109-111) 'replay the captured successful move request with E and Interview' (B's captured version reused for E; matches only by per-card-counter coincidence); (8) hro_bulk_all_or_none (:217-219) replay of the W,X,Y bulk request with V and Z — the judge has no instructed source for V/Z versions; (9) hro_bulk_places (:226-228) same with V,W,X. Where the UI hides or pre-refuses the action client-side, the replay is the ONLY server-side evidence (prompt.md:23), so the criterion becomes undecidable for the rule. Minor (P3, not the basis of the Fail): hro_refused_put_back (:136-138) does not say how to grade a UI that disables/hides the Screen->Interview control when Interview is full (no click possible, focus never moves), so a conforming client-side refusal may be scored inconsistently. Not measured: no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope says full configured grading is absent), so whether a judge spontaneously refreshes versions is unobserved.
counterexample: Broken app: authentication on all routes and the brief's mandated per-card version check (409 when the sent version != current), but the move and bulk endpoints never check role, hiring-manager job scope, one-stage skips or Interview places; its UI simply hides move controls for Observer/candidate/other managers and disables illegal moves client-side. Following the prompt literally, the judge replays Rafael's captured, already-applied move as Aud, Tomas and Bill, and replays the captured bulk request with V/Z and V/W/X carrying copied versions: every replay returns 409 'changed by someone else' and nothing moves. hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_mgr_other_job, hro_mgr_early_refused, hro_interview_full, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places (and the replay legs of hro_move_one_stage / hro_reject_hired) all score 1 although any signed-in Observer or candidate can move cards and Interview can be overfilled via the API — roughly 10+ functional weight units credited for server rules that do not exist.
suggested_fix: In functional prompt.md's replay paragraph, require every rule/role replay to first read the target cards' current state and version in a session that can see them and send that current version (a fresh, otherwise-legal request), and in the affected criteria require the refusal not to be a stale/version conflict (e.g. a role refusal 401/403/404, or a reason naming the skip/capacity/role rule), with the same fresh request succeeding for Rafael where legal as the control.
